questions.question: What is the output of print(3 * 2 ** 2)?
Which Python data structure automatically eliminates duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: Sets store unique elements; the other collection types do not generally deduplicate their elements.

questions.question:
What is printed by this code?
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(a)
questions.explanation: a and b refer to the same mutable list.

questions.question: An algorithm repeatedly halves the remaining search space in a sorted array. What is its worst-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: The number of halvings needed grows logarithmically with input length.

questions.question: A function uses def add_item(x, items=[]): and appends x to items. Why might separate calls unexpectedly share values?
options: Python recreates the list on every call
Default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined
Lists cannot be passed as arguments
questions.answer: Default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined
questions.explanation: The default list is created at function definition time and reused on calls that omit items.

questions.question: You must find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters in a string of 100,000 characters. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Sliding window with a hash map
questions.answer: Sliding window with a hash map
questions.explanation: A sliding window using last-seen positions achieves O(n) time under standard constant-time hash lookup assumptions.
